notes: Read SKILL.md, references/non-hero-scenarios.md and references/capabilities.md in full. Python guide to azure-storage-queue: DefaultAzureCredential clients, queue create/list/delete, send/receive/peek/update/delete messages, clearing queues, metadata, the async client, and binary Base64 message policies.

Medium only because SKILL.md:20 has `pip install azure-storage-queue azure-identity` (official Microsoft packages, unpinned). All queue operations are sample code for the user's application against their own storage account; credentials come from DefaultAzureCredential with placeholder account URLs, with no instruction for the agent to read or transmit secrets.

Samples include destructive service calls (delete_queue at SKILL.md:75, clear_messages at SKILL.md:169) that users should guard. SKILL.md:157-162 swallows processing exceptions with `pass`, whereas references/non-hero-scenarios.md:32-38 re-raises; the latter is the safer pattern. The async sample at SKILL.md:192 does not close its credential, contrary to the skill's own rule (fixed in non-hero-scenarios.md:68).
